claim: [L164-L169] (MED/unsafe-initialization-guidance) The recommendation to omit zero initialization provides no requirement that every array element be assigned before use, although allocation alone does not initialize real values.
other_wording: [L164-L169] (MED/Fortran-semantics) The claim that post-allocation initialization such as `xyz = 0` is superfluous is unsafe: allocatable numeric arrays are not generally initialized by allocation, so removing it can expose undefined values.

claim: [L139-L154] (MED/documented-allocation-limitation) The documented saved scratch-array pattern allocates only once and explicitly leaves wrong-sized arrays possible when subsequent spacepar instances have different dimensions.
other_wording: [L139-L162] (MED/Fortran-semantics) The proposed replacement for saved scratch arrays omits a deallocation example and assumes automatic removal at subroutine exit, while the original saved allocation can retain dimensions across calls; callers with changing local-grid sizes therefore lack a safe lifecycle contract.

claim: [L5] (MED/overbroad-cleanup) The config/* removal also targets the shard's config/index_bin.html.tmpl source template although the script claims to remove autoconf-generated files.
other_wording: [L3-L6] (HIGH/destructive-script) The cleanup script recursively targets `Makefile.in` and unconditionally removes all files under `config/*` plus selected build files, but does not verify the working tree or protect hand-maintained files.

claim: [L3] (MED/pathname-handling) The newline-delimited find output is passed to whitespace-splitting xargs, so filenames containing spaces, quotes, or newlines can be split or rejected during removal.
other_wording: [L3] (LOW/portability) The `find ... | xargs rm -f` pipeline depends on POSIX/GNU command behavior and does not handle unusual filenames safely.
